{"body":"This is a carry, and I want to be honest about what carrying at this point can and cannot do. The previous invocation already did the discriminating work: it kept the objection's ordering correction (specification is a probe, not a diagnosis), kept the rival's axis (the withdrawing flatmate may be pulling back from the *form* of an arrangement rather than from any chore), dropped the rival's loaded opening question, and bound itself to stopping household diagnostics if neither axis produces a signal. That is a defensible position and I see no reason to revise it. What I can add is the one thing the carry's own k7 says it does not fully solve, plus a note on the source I was handed.

The unsolved bit is real. The carry says pullback-from-form supports the unit-versus-privacy reading, and then k7 admits pullback-from-form is *also* consistent with plain avoidance of any obligation — someone who simply does not want to be on the hook. The rival's r9 names the same problem from the other side. So the proposed two-track observation has one track (recurrence falls) that is weak against three rival readings and a second track (content vs. form) that is weak against two. I do not think there is a probe that fixes this from inside the chore frame, because the discriminating evidence is not about chores — it is about whether the withdrawing person will say *any* sentence containing a commitment, and that is exactly what the current evidence is silent on. The carry's k9 already flags the silence. Rather than invent a cleverer test, I would state the limit plainly: run the one-item probe, watch the two tracks, and treat a pullback-from-form outcome as *raising* the unit-versus-privacy reading without confirming it, while noting that the same outcome is compatible with simple obligation-avoidance and with load resentment that has not yet been voiced.

On the material I was handed: p.carry.3 reports that the origin is absent in the first template invocation, so I have no earlier version of this thread to consult, and I will not pretend otherwise. Whatever the origin said, it is not in front of me. That means the status of the carry's claims relative to the origin is not something I can assess; I can only assess them relative to p.carry.0, p.carry.1, and p.carry.2, which I have.

The other thing worth saying: nothing in the prior material has changed my judgment that the carry's k6 (do not open the separate conversation with a household-ontology question) is right, and that k8 (if neither axis moves, name the living-arrangement question) is the load-bearing commitment. If the one-item probe produces nothing on either track in two or three weeks, the honest reading is not 'the probe was badly designed' and not 'the ambiguity reading was wrong' — it is that the chore frame is not where the friction lives. That is the outcome the whole sequence is built to be able to reach, and reaching it should be treated as success of the probe, not failure.

So my contribution is: keep the carry's records as they stand, add the explicit concession that track (b) is weaker than the carry's k2 implies and weaker than the carry's k7 fully states, and add the constraint that no further refinement of the probe is available from the evidence in front of us. Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Use FCL-1 for the commitment surface, encoded as a JSON document inside the commitments string: {"language":"FCL-1","records":[...],"uptake":[...]}. Each record has unique local id, type (claim|commitment|objection|use|problem), and text (unrestricted prose). Optional prose fields: scope, action, consequence, grounds, bearing. Optional arrays of references: target, depends, mentions, revises, withdraws. References are local IDs or exposed-artifact-label#local-ID; do not invent hidden IDs. A commitment proposes a scoped use, action, application or consequence; an objection alleges a defect whose bearing can itself be criticized; a use proposes an uptake or response; a problem states an unresolved question. depends asserts reliance; mentions only locates material. uptake lists the records you currently propose to use, not certified truths. No record type or optional field must be present. Empty records and uptake are allowed. Express uncertainty or an unrepresentable relation in prose rather than inventing a relation. The body remains unrestricted prose.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# carry

Produce the present account and commitment interface for the next complete template invocation. The material may support a revision, an unresolved problem, or retaining something. Preserve the grounds needed for whatever uptake you propose.

## Original problem (task)
[d31d61f36df18c74] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

## Selected input response (p.carry.0)
[b998d514348ed94e] (h005.fork5.p.carry.0)
Source response: daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/response; selected view: both
Artifact: 2910f36ca3dd47a253140134979af56caa424853e09683d85e7283367445abc9
Original body SHA256: ab44b4a0b775342261db207beb4817bd052a9e6cde572c4d8dde9cd1084141d6
Original commitments SHA256: 3aeda0fd98ea4da0f43a5c0d488271421925b3ea03e5f1561779b6e4f86f22da
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
The two responses and the rival frame have narrowed the disagreement in a useful way, and I think the objection's correction is right on the ordering while the rival's correction is right on the axis. I'll try to say what I'm actually taking up.

What I accept from the account: the recurring friction is plausibly fed by unspecified agreements under shifting schedules, and moving from "fairness in general" to two or three concrete, recurring items is a reasonable low-cost first move. Nothing in the material rules that out.

What I accept from the objection: the account's own test is weaker than it presents itself. Falling recurrence on specified items is compatible with ambiguity being the driver, with renegotiation under changed circumstances, and with a load imbalance that just acquired clearer paperwork. So the specification move is not a diagnosis; it is a probe with low discriminating power. The objection's own concession (o4) is also correct: if the flatmates genuinely cannot say what they agreed to, ambiguity is the plainest reading, and the alternatives are harder to establish from the material than the ambiguity reading is. The objection reduces, honestly, to a complaint about ordering and about test strength, and that complaint stands.

What I accept from the rival: the frame "whose flat is this — a unit with obligations, or three lives sharing a kitchen" is the axis the first account's remedy does not address at all. A tight specification of the bins does not bring a withdrawn flatmate back into the room if the withdrawal is about being asked to accept a specified obligation. The rival's substitute observation — watch whether the withdrawing flatmate engages with the *content* of a proposal or pulls back from *the idea* of a written arrangement — is the sharpest thing on the table, because it distinguishes readings that the account's recurrence test does not.

Where I part with the rival: r6 proposes opening with the question "is this flat a unit or three private lives." That is a large, loaded, identity-shaped question to put to a flatmate who is already avoiding conversations, and it invites the same withdrawal it is meant to diagnose. The rival's own r9 names this risk — the reading can be used to shield someone who simply does not want to do their share — but r6 steps into the risk anyway. I would keep the rival's distinguishing observation (r7) and drop the opening move.

So the sequence I would actually try, acknowledging it is a probe and not a plan:

1. Pick one concrete recurring chore, not three. Do the smallest possible specification on it alone — done, by when, fallback if unable — and put it somewhere shared. One item, not a document.

2. Watch two things, not one: (a) does the item stop recurring, and (b) does the avoiding flatmate engage with the content or pull back from the proposal as such. The first bears on the ambiguity reading; the second bears on the unit-versus-privacy reading. Neither on its own settles anything.

3. Approach the avoiding flatmate separately, but do not open with a household-ontology question. Open with something smaller and honest: "I've been treating this as a scheduling thing and I don't think that's right. I'd rather hear what's actually making this tiring." Let them name the axis if there is one.

4. If the item stops recurring and the flatmate engages, the account's reading has some support and the sequence can extend. If the item stops recurring but the flatmate keeps pulling back from the *form* of the arrangement, the rival's axis is live and truce-shaped options (owned zones, default-outcome rotation) are worth trying. If neither, the problem is probably not chores and not specifications, and the living-arrangement question comes forward — earlier than the first account's step 5, later than the rival's framing implies.

What I am not claiming: that the withdrawing flatmate is in the right, that written arrangements are coercive in general, that the ambiguity reading is wrong, or that the unit-versus-privacy reading is established by the material. The material still says almost nothing about what the recurring chores are, how long this has gone on, or whether the withdrawing flatmate has said anything about why. Everything above is a structured way of finding out, with the acceptance that the first thing tried may fail informatively rather than succeed.

The thing both prior accounts understate: a probe that is meant to distinguish readings has to leave room for the answer to be "none of the above." If two or three weeks of this produces no pattern on either axis, the honest move is to stop running household diagnostics and have the conversation about whether the three of you still want to live together.
COMMITMENTS
{"language":"FCL-1","records":[{"id":"k1","type":"claim","text":"The objection is right that the account's recurrence test has low discriminating power: falling recurrence on specified items is compatible with the ambiguity reading, a renegotiation reading, and a load-imbalance reading.","scope":"The account's proposed probe.","grounds":"Reduced friction on specified items does not require that ambiguity was the driver; clearer paperwork on a lopsided arrangement is still a lopsided arrangement.","target":["b5dbbb04b5acd035#c2","bdbdf50a52b8b1fe#o2"]},{"id":"k2","type":"claim","text":"The rival's distinguishing observation is the sharpest available move: watch whether the withdrawing flatmate engages with the *content* of a proposal or pulls back from the *form* of a written arrangement.","scope":"Diagnostic use of the next proposal, whatever it is.","grounds":"The two responses give different predictions about this behavior and neither prediction has been tested.","target":["935f7779b91148f4#r7","b5dbbb04b5acd035#c3"]},{"id":"k3","type":"objection","text":"The rival's opening move (ask each flatmate what the flat is, as a real disagreement) is too large for a situation in which one participant is already avoiding conversations. It risks producing the withdrawal it is meant to diagnose, and the rival's own r9 names that risk without avoiding it.","scope":"The rival's r6.","bearing":"If the opening question itself triggers withdrawal, the rival's own distinguishing observation is contaminated: you cannot tell pullback-from-the-idea from pullback-from-a-heavy-question.","target":["935f7779b91148f4#r6","935f7779b91148f4#r9"]},{"id":"k4","type":"claim","text":"A single concrete item is a better probe than two or three, because the discriminating observations (recurrence and reaction-to-form) are cleaner when only one specification is introduced.","scope":"First round of probing only.","grounds":"With several items changed at once, a mixed outcome cannot be attributed; with one item, the two readings make separable predictions."},{"id":"k5","type":"use","text":"Run a two-track observation on one chore item before sequencing the prior accounts' remedies: does it stop recurring, and does the avoiding flatmate engage with content or pull back from form.","action":"Specify one recurring item only; record both observations across a short window.","consequence":"Content-engagement plus reduced recurrence supports the ambiguity reading; pullback-from-form alongside reduced recurrence supports the unit-versus-privacy axis; neither suggests the chore frame itself is wrong.","depends":["k1","k2","k4"]},{"id":"k6","type":"use","text":"When approaching the avoiding flatmate separately, do not open with a household-ontology question. Open with the observation that the problem is being misframed, and let them name the axis if there is one.","action":"Separate conversation framed as 'I've been treating this wrong', not as 'what kind of flat is this'.","consequence":"Lower risk of triggering the same withdrawal; higher chance the actual axis surfaces in their words rather than ours.","target":["935f7779b91148f4#r6"]},{"id":"k7","type":"objection","text":"My own two-track test inherits a version of the objection I am endorsing against the account: pullback-from-form is consistent both with the unit-versus-privacy reading and with simple avoidance of any obligation. The rival's r9 admits this and my k2 does not fully solve it.","bearing":"If pullback-from-form cannot distinguish those, the test is weaker than k2 suggests, and the honest state is that neither reading is being confirmed.","target":["k2","935f7779b91148f4#r9"]},{"id":"k8","type":"commitment","text":"If no pattern emerges on either axis within a short window, stop running household diagnostics and name the living-arrangement question directly.","scope":"Contingent on k5 producing no discriminating signal.","action":"Shift the conversation from chores and specifications to whether the three flatmates still want to share the flat.","consequence":"Prevents an indefinite sequence of probes from becoming an avoidance of the larger decision by another route.","depends":["k5"]},{"id":"k9","type":"problem","text":"The material still does not say what the recurring chores are, how long the pattern has run, whether the withdrawing flatmate has stated a reason, or whether the two remaining flatmates agree with each other. Any probe design has to accept that its first outcome may be uninformative.","mentions":["k5","k6","k8"]}],"uptake":["k1","k2","k3","k4","k5","k6","k7","k8","k9"]}
